```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Each completed data set is fitted on its own design. The fits are pooled with Rubin's rules. The design degrees of freedom are the complete-data degrees of freedom.

```{r, include = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("mitools", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::knit_exit()
```

```{r setup}
library(svysem)
base <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = 2)$variables
second <- base
second$y1 <- second$y1 + 0.15
second$y3 <- second$y3 - 0.10
design <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~psu, strata = ~strat, weights = ~w,
  data = mitools::imputationList(list(base, second))
)
```

The model labels a residual covariance and defines its Fisher *z* with `atanh()`. That defined parameter is pooled on the *z* scale.

```{r fit}
model <- "
  f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
  y1 ~~ v1*y1
  y2 ~~ v2*y2
  y1 ~~ c*y2
  z := atanh(c / sqrt(v1 * v2))
"
fit <- svycfa(model, design)
coef(fit)
```

`pooled_estimates()` reports the Rubin estimate, its standard error, and the Barnard-Rubin degrees of freedom. `standardized = TRUE` pools correlations on the Fisher *z* scale and transforms them back. `pooled_wald()` takes the same constraints as `lavaan::lavTestWald()`. `fitMeasures()` pools the scaled chi-square and summarizes the robust indices by their mean, minimum, and maximum. Those indices are not pooled with Rubin's rules.

```{r pool}
head(pooled_estimates(fit), 3)
pooled_wald(fit, "z == 0")
fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq.scaled", "cfi.robust.mean", "cfi.robust.min", "cfi.robust.max"))
```

The status table has one row per imputation. `on_fail = "omit"` drops a failed imputation and records the message, as long as two fits remain. The default is `"stop"`.

```{r status}
fit@status
```
